title: US distributor of China’s popular humanoid robots shifts to domestic production after import ban
summary: RoboStore, a leading US distributor of Chinese-made humanoid and quadruped robots from Unitree Robotics, is pivoting to domestic manufacturing due to US government restrictions on foreign-made robots. The company plans to open a 66,000-square-foot facility in New York by early 2027 to produce commercial robots, including healthcare-focused humanoid torsos, security quadrupeds, and educational platforms. The shift follows legislative actions like the American Security Robotics Act and an FCC ban on imports of certain foreign robots, citing cybersecurity concerns. RoboStore aims to address industry-specific needs rather than relying on general-purpose humanoid robots.
key_points: RoboStore was the main North American distributor for Unitree Robotics' affordable humanoid and quadruped robots, serving universities (Harvard, MIT) and tech companies (Amazon, Nvidia, OpenAI).
The US government imposed restrictions on foreign-made robots, including an FCC ban on imports of Unitree’s models, citing national security and cybersecurity risks.

RoboStore shut down its distribution business and launched **Robo Inc.** to manufacture robots domestically in a 66,000-square-foot facility on Long Island, targeting commercial production by Q1 2027.
New products under development include: a wheeled humanoid torso for healthcare, a security-focused quadruped, and a humanoid platform for education/research.
The company aims to raise funding after years of bootstrapping, leveraging demand from existing customers for US-compliant robotics solutions.
RoboStore’s CEO emphasizes that specialized robotic arms (e.g., from Standard Bots, Universal Robots) may be more practical for businesses than general-purpose humanoid robots.
